findings.title: Template variables and ad hoc filters are applied twice in the split path
findings.body:
`runSplitQuery` now runs `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on every target. Each sub-request is built as `{ ...request, range, targets }`, so it still carries `scopedVars` and `filters`. `datasource.runQuery()` then calls `super.query()` (DataSourceWithBackend), which runs `applyTemplateVariables(q, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` again on the already-interpolated targets.

`applyTemplateVariables` is not idempotent:
- `addAdHocFilters` → `addLabelToQuery` only de-duplicates when the filter goes into the stream selector. When the query has a parser or existing label filters, it appends ` | key=`value`` with no duplicate check. For example, `{app="x"} | json` with an ad hoc filter `level=error` becomes `{app="x"} | json | level=`error` | level=`error``. That query is what reaches Loki and what users see in the query inspector.
- A second `templateSrv.replace` pass also re-interpolates variable values. Suppose a textbox line-filter value contains `$host` and `host` is also a dashboard variable; the literal text gets substituted on the second pass.

Before this PR, interpolation happened only once, in `super.query`. Possible fixes: interpolate only what the splitting logic needs (e.g. `step` for `calculateStep`), or strip `filters` from the request passed downstream after interpolating.

findings.title: Shard path now interpolates and applies ad hoc filters three times
findings.body:
`runShardSplitQuery` now calls `applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)`. The previous `interpolateVariablesInQueries` call did not pass filters, so ad hoc filters were not applied at this stage before.

It then passes `{ ...request, targets }` (with `filters` intact) to `runSplitQuery`. That function now calls `applyTemplateVariables` again on every sub-request. `runQuery` → `super.query` applies it a third time.

For queries with a parser or label filters, each ad hoc filter is appended three times to the expression sent to Loki. Variable values are also re-templated twice. The updated test asserting `applyTemplateVariables` was called 5 times (1 + 4 sub-requests) codifies this redundant re-interpolation instead of catching it. Interpolation should happen once, e.g. by clearing `filters` on the request handed to `runSplitQuery`, or by having `runSplitQuery` skip interpolation when called from the shard path.

findings.title: New interpolation test asserts `$__auto` frontend substitution that doesn't happen in production
findings.body:
The new test 'Interpolates queries before execution' stubs `templateSrv.replace` to unconditionally replace `$__auto` with `5m`. It then asserts that the expression sent to `runQuery` is `count_over_time({a="b"}[5m])`. The real `LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables` deliberately strips `__auto` (and `__range*`, `__interval*`) from scopedVars so these are interpolated on the backend. In production `$__auto` stays as-is.

The test therefore documents behaviour that doesn't exist. The same pattern is copied into `shardQuerySplitting.test.ts` (around line 88). Neither test covers the realistic case: a dashboard variable in `step` affecting `calculateStep` grouping, or ad hoc filters combined with splitting. As a result they would not catch the duplicated-filter regression.
